clue.text: Type of book it is difficult to endorse

parts.note: difficult means hard
to endorse a person or plan is to back it

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain kind of book is hard to give their approval to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it is' is a link joining definition and wordplay; 'endorse' looks like signing a cheque but means support.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound volume with stiff covers is a recognised format of published book.

clue.text: Showered with cries of acclamation

definitions.meaning: greeted with enthusiastic shouts of welcome

explanation.definitionFit: Ice pellets falling means showered down, and greeting someone joyfully means acclaiming them.

clue.text: Automatic umpire on Roman law

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is an umpire
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: An umpire automatically applies the rules of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second. LEX is Latin, the language of Roman law.
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary response done without thought is automatic.

clue.text: Local advocates?

parts.note: a local is a pub, and the staff behind its counter could be called members of the bar, as lawyers are

explanation.surface: Someone asks about neighbourhood lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's regular pub; barristers are said to belong to the bar, as do those who serve drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who serve behind the counter of a pub work at the bar, as barristers do in court.

clue.text: Generous daily help, albeit disorganised

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a daily cleaner

indicators.note: disorganised means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is kind-hearted even though she is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is British for a cleaning woman; 'disorganised' rearranges ALBEIT into ITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving freely to those in need is being kind and open-handed.

clue.text: Dramatic events portrayed by one in Ealing area

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for one sits inside the name of the London district

parts.note: Acton is a district in the London borough of Ealing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stars in a drama filmed in a part of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London in the borough of Ealing, also home of the famous film studios, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting incidents in a story or film are what audiences call the plot's exploits and happenings.

clue.text: Understand the significance of wearing a natural fibre

parts.note: cotton is a natural plant fibre
if you have something on, you are wearing it

explanation.surface: Someone realises why it matters to dress in cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; COTTON ON is British slang for catch on.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch on to an idea is to grasp its meaning at last, an informal idiom.

clue.text: I can describe it as suitable for copying

indicators.note: describe means draw round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: I can means I am able, contracted to I'm able

explanation.surface: Someone claims they can call it worthy of emulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is used in the geometric sense of drawing a line around; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being reproduced or mimicked means fit to be copied.

clue.text: Recoil of a gun strikes a right winger as trifling

indicators.note: recoil means springing backwards, so the word for the firearm is reversed

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A firearm's kick hits a Conservative politician, but only slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoil of' turns GUN into NUG; 'strikes' is a link. TORY is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Of no real value or worth, ineffective and trivial.

clue.text: Unofficial brief to a Liberal

parts.note: to brief someone is to inform them

explanation.surface: A party official sends instructions to a Liberal politician off the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like an adjective meaning short, but it is the verb, to give instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something casual and not sanctioned by authority is unofficial, lacking formal standing.

clue.text: Way to call up a computer sequence

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way or road
to call someone up on the phone is to ring them

explanation.surface: Someone describes how to dial into a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' gives ST, the usual abbreviation for street; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In programming, a run of characters treated as one unit of data is called by this name.

clue.text: Critical appraisal of a theologian

parts.note: describes the close interpretive study a scholar of religion makes of scripture

explanation.surface: A reviewer assesses the work of a scholar of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names critical interpretation of a text, especially of the Bible, the classic task of a divinity scholar.

clue.text: Firm Latvian, for instance, is true-blue

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a Latvian is an example of a Balt, a native of the Baltic states

explanation.surface: A company employee from Latvia is described as loyal through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'true-blue' suggests staunch loyalty but here means a genuinely blue colour; 'is' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal gives its name to a deep, pure shade of blue pigment used by painters and potters.

clue.text: Sets up cash-register in fixed position

parts.note: to set up something is to stand it
a till is a cash-register

explanation.surface: A shop installs a till in a permanent spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt means stopping where one is, motionless.

clue.text: He's quick to take over

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so this describes a speedy player who bowls them

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to seize control of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled by one player; 'take over' looks like seizing control.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who delivers the ball at high pace is the quick one who takes a set of six balls.

clue.text: Star arising from the East by chance

indicators.note: by means one piece is placed next to the other
arising from suggests something emerging changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a risk is a chance of something happening

explanation.surface: A star rises in the east as if by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising from' rearranges EAST into ASTE, and 'by' places RISK beside it; 'the' is a link. The surface evokes the star of Bethlehem.
explanation.definitionFit: The typographic mark shaped like a little star is named from the Greek for small star.

clue.text: Put the squeeze on a fellow journalist

parts.note: to press is to squeeze
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone pressures a colleague who works as a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the squeeze on' reads as intimidation; it is simply PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper reporter belongs to the press, the news trade.

clue.text: Cause disturbance in fashion able North Yorkshire market town

parts.note: U means upper-class, hence acceptable and fashionable
Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A trendy northern market town is thrown into turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: U is an old label for upper-class, so fashionable; SETTLE is a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset or unsettle a calm state means to disrupt or make uneasy.

clue.text: Resolute course of action taken by the big-game angler

definitions.meaning: a firm, unwavering policy or stance
a sturdy fishing cord that a sea fisherman needs for large fish

explanation.definitionFit: A firm policy is a tough stance, and a heavy-duty fishing cord is what one uses to land marlin or shark.

clue.text: Family stress

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or breed

explanation.definitionFit: A lineage or breed is a stock, and tension or pressure is a strain on someone.

clue.text: Grumble if it's not served on the glorious Twelfth

definitions.text: if it's not served on the glorious Twelfth
definitions.meaning: the 12th of August opens the British shooting season for this game bird, so diners complain if it is missing

explanation.walkthrough: The Glorious Twelfth is 12 August, when shooting of the red game bird opens in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to grumble, and the moorland game bird is shot from 12 August.

clue.text: On what did Doctor Doolittle place emphasis?

definitions.text: On what did Doctor Doolittle place emphasis?

parts.words: On what did Doctor Doolittle place emphasis?
parts.note: Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion has her speech doctored by Professor Higgins, and stress on a syllable is a kind of emphasis

explanation.surface: A question about what the animal-talking doctor stressed most.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Doctor Dolittle, but the spelling points to Eliza Doolittle, whose Cockney speech is reformed in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress laid on a syllable is emphasis, and a regional manner of speech is what Eliza had corrected.

clue.text: Followed Susanna in the last resort

indicators.note: in places the short form of the woman's name inside the word for the final stage

parts.note: in the last resort means finally, in the end
Sue is a short form of the name Susanna

explanation.surface: Susanna went along after others, as a final fallback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the last resort' reads as an idiom for finally, and the surface treats it as one phrase; here 'in' is the container signal and 'the last resort' alone gives the final stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that came after, as a result, are said to have followed on.

clue.text: Secret coteries broken up

indicators.note: a group broken up is scattered, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Exclusive cliques have been disbanded and their secrets with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' rearranges the letters of COTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge meant only for a small, initiated circle is obscure and hidden from outsiders.

clue.text: I meant to resettle one of the occupants

indicators.note: to resettle is to move somewhere new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone intended to move one of the residents to a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resettle' rearranges the letters of I MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in an institution such as a prison or hostel is one of its residents.

clue.text: Set the record straight about Underworld malpractice

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for that realm
abuse is improper or wrongful practice

explanation.surface: Someone corrects the facts about wrongdoing in criminal circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests gangsters but gives DIS, the classical underworld; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from a false belief is to correct their mistaken idea of the facts.

clue.text: Livingstone and Murray back in the doghouse

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London

indicators.note: back means the name of the union leader is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Len Murray, former General Secretary of the Trades Union Congress

explanation.surface: Two left-wing political figures find themselves out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEN (Len Murray, British trade union leader) into NEL; 'in the doghouse' looks like disgrace but the doghouse is a literal dog's shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hut for a pet hound is its shelter, a literal dog's house.

clue.text: Mournful spy absorbs the information

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for the spy takes the information into its middle

parts.note: a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A sad secret agent soaks up intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintive, resonant sound such as a lament is described this way.
